observed_behavior: Original ready workers lost their checkout before attachment and could not invoke canonical recovery.
expected_behavior: The proven original worker can reconstruct its exact checkout and finish adoption and attachment without replacement.
causal_mechanism: Recovery ownership was recorded only after attachment, although attachment depended on successful filesystem bootstrap.

anti_pattern.structural_description: Recovery authority for an interrupted prerequisite depended on completing the later lifecycle transition.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: An interrupted bootstrap cannot satisfy the attachment prerequisite needed to authorize its own repair.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: Durable proven native identity authorizes exact-path bootstrap repair without falsely claiming authenticated attachment.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: PROVISIONED enrolls immutable original identity and source on the started creation; its original capability uses the shared reconstruction engine at the detached dispatch checkpoint.

applicability_conditions: Native creation succeeds before local adoption and authenticated ownership attachment.
known_non_matches: Already attached workers retain branch-bound recovery authority.
confirmation_evidence: Supported host inspection identified both original ready sessions and absent native checkouts; fail-first real-Git recovery rejected their missing attachment binding.
regression_proofs: tests/worker-worktrees.test.js: provisioned original worker recovers before adoption and attachment without replacing its started creation
